panel: 8 lenses (naive-visitor, humanizer, curator, interaction, a11y, mobile, fact, historian) + chair, run against production
verdict: The rebuild holds up as a museum piece in its bones. Every lens independently found the fundamentals sound: the fact-registry audit passes with 220 resolving daggers, the court holdings are stated with legal precision, chapter 4 is handled with restraint, the a11y and interaction skeletons verified clean under live driving, and the prose passes every hard AI-tell screen. But it cannot ship as-is, for five reasons the panel treats as blockers. The phone experience is physically broken (a 456px layout at 375px viewports, caught independently by two lenses) and the exhibit's central gesture, tapping a graded area, selects an effectively random neighborhood on touch. The finale misquotes its own promised closing question one screen after promising it (two lenses). The single most load-bearing statistic resolves, at the moment of maximum visitor scrutiny, to the site citing its own draft JSON file by internal filename (two lenses, and the grep shows at least five source records carry the same internal locator). And the opening panel reasserts a categorical HOLC claim the project's own factcheck had already softened, falsifiable from the exhibit's own reading room. Below the blockers, the defects concentrate in exactly two seams: facts.json source-record hygiene (duplicate bibliography entries, Wikipedia behind headline stats, a leaked editorial TODO) and wall text that outruns the registry (miscounts, a spliced quotation, unregistered attributions, causal superlatives). All of it is finish work on a structure worth finishing; nothing in the punch list touches the concept.

lensOveralls.overall: To a stranger who knows nothing about redlining or Chicago, this exhibit is genuinely legible and often excellent. The what/when/why plates, the plain first-use definitions of covenant, contract sale, kitchenette, and Black Belt, the content advisory with a skip control, the honest empty states ('No surveyor sheet survives'), and the period-language chips all do exactly what the design intent asks; the failures are at the edges, where unexplained vocabulary (REPORTED, HOLC, TIF, 'the lamp', 'mechanism rules'), a seven-doors-versus-six promise, a 40-versus-32 pin overstatement, and a finale that poses a different question than the one it just promised chip away at an otherwise trustworthy voice.

The exhibit passes the hard AI-tell screens cleanly across every user-visible surface swept (walltext.json, all room content modules, station chrome, machines/cases/ledger/voices data, facts.json displays, and the rendered production page): zero em-dashes, zero sentence-internal colons, no AI vocabulary, no negative parallelism, no trailing -ing analyses, and no generic uplift endings, and the 13 chapters of wall text genuinely read as edited historian prose. The residue that remains is a softer, second-order tell, a habit of manufactured two-beat punchlines and imperative fragments concentrated in the machine-conceit chrome (machine definitions, room leads, case verdicts), which is survivable but worth one flattening pass because the pattern repeats often enough for a suspicious reader to notice.

The rebuild genuinely reads as a museum exhibit now, and the hardest things are done right: ch4 is handled with restraint and dignity, the Mapping Inequality CC BY-NC attribution rides every map surface including the files room, period-language warning chips are applied consistently, verbatim quotes are policed apart from paraphrase, and the machine rooms hold real documents (Article 34 verbatim, the HOLC form and sheet D74, the case files) with honest plates where the record is incomplete. What remains is credibility finish rather than concept: a colophon whose 91-source bibliography contains visible duplicates and Wikipedia entries behind headline statistics, a finale that misquotes its own closing question, a few checkable miscounts (six rooms vs seven doors, forty located vs 32 pins, ten chapters vs twelve), and three or four surviving game-register strings ('Life happens', 'one event per visit', 'The Answer Key', 'ships after counsel review') that a curator would strike on first walkthrough.

The interaction skeleton is genuinely strong. Doors, room close paths, Escape, browser Back and Forward, sheet permalinks, the copy-link button, grade chips, search, show-more, deep links including bogus ids, and the desktop timeline all behaved correctly under live driving with zero console errors. The two things that would embarrass the exhibit are both mobile-shaped, a horizontal overflow that clips the chapter sheet and docket on every phone, and touch targets on the HOLC map so small that the exhibit's central gesture selects the wrong neighborhood, plus one desktop trap where a first-visit rail jump lands a screen short of the chapter it claims to have reached.

Accessibility fundamentals are genuinely strong and mostly verified live on production: one h1 with a clean no-skip heading tree, labeled landmarks, a properly trapped and focus-returning room dialog (Escape and Back both land on the originating door), a roving-tabindex HOLC map that turns 674 areas into one tab stop with arrow keys and a visible focus ring, all 32 bombing marks keyboard-operable with descriptive names, consistent aria-pressed/aria-expanded on toggles, accurate figure alt text (checked against the actual images), sliders with aria-valuetext, and a soft-ink token that passes contrast at 7.6:1. The two things worth fixing before ship are the dead reduced-motion CSS hook (the state mirrors the preference but no element ever carries .exhibit-root plus data-motion=off, so VoiceCard, TwoBuyers, and FollowTheDollar still animate for reduced-motion visitors and partially inside the no-motion ch4) and the silent sheet-open interaction in the Surveyor's Files, plus a cluster of sub-4.5:1 micro-type at ink alphas 45 to 60 percent.

The reading experience itself is strong on a phone, the wall text, plates, docket lists, files room, answer wall, and sheet permalinks all hold up at 390px, but the page currently ships with a real 66-96px horizontal overflow at mobile widths, traced to the ch4 bombing docket grid and the station header title, which clips the docket dates, the station title, the room text, and the era chip depending on browser. Fix that one layout bug plus the two amputated reference tables and the too-small HOLC map taps, and this is a genuinely good mobile exhibit.

The provenance machinery is genuinely sound: the audit gate passes clean, all 220 rendered daggers resolve to the registry, tier badges and the Mapping Inequality attribution render everywhere required, the record table matches facts.json verbatim, the 91-source bibliography count is accurate and its links work (the two 403s are bot walls, not dead links), and the #room-files permalink lands on the right sheet. The failures are concentrated in individual source records, and one is a p1: a wall-text claim whose visitor-facing citation is the site citing its own draft JSON file, plus a leaked editorial TODO and six visible bibliography duplicates under a colophon that promises de-duplication.

The exhibit's spine is genuinely strong from this lens, and the chair should protect the legally precise court holdings (Buchanan, Corrigan, Hansberry, Shelley, each stated with exactly what it did and did not do), the disciplined use of corrected registry figures (44,000 not 40,000 for 1910, the 155-contracts floor with 'renegotiations continued past that count', the 46 and 17 percent scoped honestly to Hyde Park A and B), and the sourcing honesty on the armor paraphrase, the Kimpton quotation, and Baldwin's nationally framed answer. The defects cluster where wall text outruns the exhibit's own evidence chain, namely an opening HOLC claim the project's factcheck had already softened, a site-internal 1938 versus 1939-40 dating contradiction, a spliced Article 34 quotation the exhibit's own machine room contradicts verbatim, and a handful of unregistered attributions and causal superlatives (Travis, the servants pledge, the map explaining lender unanimity) that a specialist would catch first.

disposition: All 31 items fixed across three ownership-partitioned agents (data, stations, shell/rooms) plus coordinator integration. Suite 133/133, audit 111 facts clean, build clean.
